key_insight: MLLMs struggle to localize retinal OCT biomarkers, but OCT-specific fine-tuning raised grounding F1 from 23.7% to 33.9%.
clinical_relevance: Localizing reported findings could make image-based AI outputs easier to verify, but these results do not establish readiness for clinical use.
method: Introduced RetinaGroundBench with ophthalmologist-annotated biomarker bounding boxes.
Proposed AggIoU to assess combined coverage from overlapping predicted boxes.
Evaluated 27 open-source MLLMs and fine-tuned the 8B-parameter RetGrounder using OCT grounding and text.
evidence_signal: The benchmark includes 815 B-scans, 4,537 bounding boxes, 13 biomarkers and 8 diseases; RetGrounder achieved 33.9% grounding F1 versus 23.7% for the best general-purpose model, a 43% relative improvement.
watch_item: Grounding performance remains limited, and biomarker presence accuracy should not be mistaken for reliable localization.
paper_title: A Visual Grounding Benchmark for Retinal OCT with Multimodal Large Language Models
